title.narrative: Provision of cash for energy needs to support extremely vulnerable households ahead of winter in eastern Ukraine

description.narrative: ltpgtThe war in Ukraine has caused a severe humanitarian crisis, resulting in extreme human suffering and increased needs. The intensification of hostilities, including the use of antipersonnel landmines, has worsened the situation, and the approaching harsh winter threatens to exacerbate it further. ltbrgtAs the situation continues to increase pre-existing vulnerabilities and deplete resources and with winter around the corner, households in the eastern side of the country are expected to face difficulties meeting their winter needs. To address some of these gaps, the International Rescue Committee (IRC) and its partners, Pomogaem and Peaceful Heaven of Kharkiv (PHK), propose to deliver life-saving winterization assistance to households (HHs) in Kharkivska, Zaporizka, and Donetska oblasts, with a focus on HHs in rural areas close to the frontline or in newly accessible locations. The assistance, provided through a cash modality, aims to support a total of 1,712 HHs (approximately 3,424 individuals) and meet their heating needs during the coldest winter months. ltbrgtIn line with the Shelter/NFI (S/NFI) Cluster’s 2024-2025 Ukraine Winterization Recommendations, the project will prioritize HHs with elderly people (55+) or HHs that have people with disabilities or injuries. At a time when access to resources is limited due to an increase in the cost of living, loss of income, and depletion of savings, the project will ensure that beneficiaries can stay in a warm and safe environment. Through collaborative design with partners and active community engagement, the IRC and its partners will identify the most vulnerable communities in hard-to-reach rural areas near the frontline and determine the best methods and practices for providing cash assistance for winterization, helping these communities afford the increased energy costs. Coordination will ensure that all activities align with the Shelter NFI Cluster guidelines and include active engagement with the Cluster, national partners, and local authorities, such as Oblast Administrations, hromada authorities, and departments of social policy. This collaboration aims to ensure that the IRC, Pomogaem, and PHK deliver quality assistance to affected individuals, upholding safety and dignity during the peak of winter. ltbrgtlt/pgt
